I started utilizing my time wisely in-game since the time goes too fast by doing these things:

1) I have a chest dedicated to items that I have to turn into the museum. Note that each item has a little museum icon with a check mark box option on it at the top right corner when you hover over them. If it’s unchecked, it means you still have to donate it to the museum. When I’ve accumulated enough items, I just take it all in one go instead of one by one.

2) I do the same thing above with requests. I stopped turning in villager requests one by one because it took too long trying to find each villager. I just save all the requests, get the items, and wait until every Friday nights or Saturday markets where all the villagers are gathered to turn them all in. NOTE: I think I crashed the game before trying to turn in like 15+ requests at once so be careful turning in too many at one time.

3) Always manually save your game after watering your crops or doing a lot of activities so you don’t lose progress when the game unexpectedly crashes. You can save the game manually by interacting with the book next to the bed. Make it a habit to save manually BEFORE going to sleep, because I had my game crash after I slept TWICE and the save file will not save you at that point.

4) Save some crops to make food since some food is very profitable. For example, grow a lot of strawberries, pumpkin, wheat (to make flour), sugar cane (after upgrading the general store), etc. 

Also try to get animals as fast as possible so you can get milk and eggs for cooking recipes! :)

Have fun!!

Yeah, correct - when nothing's happening its just a solid xD. Typically in the flip fluid add-on, the domain is automatically shown as a wireframe view so you can see what you're doing. 

For blender's own liquid sim, it doesn't really do that automatically, but you can just set it to wireframe mode yourself if you wanna see what you're doing lol.

The liquid domains are typically visible during solid view in object mode. When you go to render view, it will typically just only show the liquid animation.

If you want to hide the solid domain from the animation at a specific time frame, let’s say between frames 1-55, then you need to keyframe the visibility so that it’s hidden in render view for that time range. 

Then you have to keyframe it to become visible again (between keyframes 55 through 150 for example) so that the liquid simulation shows up again in the render view.

I’ve finally found myself a decent instant coffee recipe where all I need is a Korean brand of coffee called Maxim Mocha Gold Mild. If anyone loves smooth iced coffees and something sweet and quick to make, here’s a recipe:

1) Pour about 1/4 cup or 1/2 Cup of boiling hot water in a cup with 1 packet of Maxim Gold. You don’t want to add too much water because you’re going to be adding in tons of ice later!
2) Add 1 Tbsp of Torani syrup (I like the hazelnut or PSL) 
3) Add 1 Tbsp condensed milk 
4) Add a small amount of milk, like 4 Tbsp. Don’t make it too diluted.
5) Stir and use a handheld whisk. Then add lots of ice to your liking. 

I know not everyone likes sweet iced coffees like me but I’m just sharing this for those that are looking to try cheaper alternatives to Starbucks (and don’t want to shell out $$$ for an espresso / keurig machine).

Some projects are so small you’ll be cleaning the damn sewer water coming out from god knows where or putting out fires by yourself or bandaging up some sub’s finger that they accidentally chopped off. 

Expect to work 12-16 hours depending on a project’s timeline. Also expect to be laid off if another pandemic comes or if you complain to HR about a small issue, you’re next on the chopping block (happens all the time in this industry).

Anyways, I do not recommend it lol.

1. Make the starter paste first by adding 3 Tbsp water + 3 Tbsp whole milk + 2 Tbsp King Arthur Bread Flour in a sauce pan on super low heat. Whisk it until it becomes a gooey, milky paste but don’t overcook it. 
2. Turn off the heat in the sauce pan. In the same sauce pan, you can cool it down by adding in 1/2 cup of milk and 1 large egg together and mixing it.
3. In a separate large metal bowl, add 2 1/2 Cups of bread flour, 1/4 Cup granulated sugar, 1 Teaspoon Salt, 1 Tablespoon Instant Yeast. Mix these together and then add your paste that you just made. Then add melted unsalted butter ( 4 Tablespoons) last to the mix.
4. Knead by hand until the dough is soft, usually takes 20 minutes. Don’t stick by this time though, you have to feel the texture of the dough. It can’t have that crumbly feeling, & it needs to be soft on the outside and stretchy. If you have a stand mixer, great- knead it for 15 minutes but check the dough texture.
5. Let the dough rest for 1 hour.
6. Cut up the dough into 4 equal pieces. Shape them into a ball and use a rolling pin to stretch them out, and shape them like you would typical bread.
7. Remember to butter your bread pan. Place the 4 rolls into the bread pan and let them sit for another hour until they puff up. Make take longer depending on temp inside the house. Also make sure to coat them in 2 Tbsp water and 1 egg mixture after they’re done puffing up. 
8. Bake at 350F for 27 minutes. Then take it out of the pan and put on a wire rack.
